title: Friedelin Attenuates Neuronal Dysfunction and Memory Impairment by Inhibition of the Activated JNK/NF-kappaB Signalling Pathway in Scopolamine-Induced Mice Model of Neurodegeneration.
authors: Sandhu, Marva; Irfan, Hafiz Muhammad; Shah, Shahid Ali; Ahmed, Madiha; Naz, Iffat; Akram, Muhammad; Fatima, Humaira; Farooq, Ayesha Shuja
one_liner_zh: 该文研究friedelin对东莨菪碱诱导小鼠神经退行性变的保护作用，涉及JNK/NF-kB信号通路和分子对接，但核心是神经药理学而非蛋白质-DNA互作，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Oxidative stress (OS) and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) are both key indicators implicated in neuro-inflammatory signalling pathways and their respective neurodegenerative diseases. Drugs targeting these factors can be considered as suitable candidates for treatment of neuronal dysfunction and memory impairment. The present study encompasses beneficial effects of a naturally occurring triterpenoid, friedelin, against scopolamine-induced oxidative stress and neurodegenerative pathologies in mice models. The treated animals were subjected to behavioural tests i.e., Y-maze and Morris water maze (MWM) for memory dysfunction. The underlying mechanism was determined via western blotting, antioxidant enzymes and lipid profile analyses. Molecular docking studies were carried out to predict the binding modes of friedelin in the binding pocket of p-JNK protein. The results reveal that scopolamine caused oxidative stress by (1) inhibiting catalase (CAT), peroxidase enzyme (POD), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and reduced glutathione enzyme (GSH); (2) the up-regulation of thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) in mice brain; and (3) affecting the neuronal synapse (both pre- and post-synapse) followed by associated memory dysfunction. In contrast, friedelin administration not only abolished scopolamine-induced oxidative stress, glial cell activation, and neuro-inflammation but also inhibited p-JNK and NF-kappaB and their downstream signaling molecules. Moreover, friedelin administration improved neuronal synapse and reversed scopolamine-induced memory impairment accompanied by the inhibition of beta-secretase enzyme (BACE-1) to halt amyloidogenic pathways of amyloid-beta production. In summary, all of the results show that friedelin is a potent naturally isolated neuro-therapeutic agent to reverse scopolamine-induced neuropathology, which is characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract_zh: 氧化应激（OS）和c-Jun N末端激酶（JNK）均是参与神经炎症信号通路及其相关神经退行性疾病的关键指标。针对这些因素的药物可被视为治疗神经元功能障碍和记忆障碍的合适候选药物。本研究探讨了天然存在的三萜类化合物木栓酮（friedelin）对小鼠模型中东莨菪碱诱导的氧化应激和神经退行性病理的有益作用。处理后的动物接受了行为测试，即Y迷宫和莫里斯水迷宫（MWM），以评估记忆功能障碍。通过蛋白质印迹法、抗氧化酶和脂质谱分析确定了潜在机制。进行了分子对接研究，以预测木栓酮在p-JNK蛋白结合口袋中的结合模式。结果表明，东莨菪碱通过以下方式引起氧化应激：（1）抑制过氧化氢酶（CAT）、过氧化物酶（POD）、超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和还原型谷胱甘肽酶（GSH）；（2）上调小鼠脑中的硫代巴比妥酸反应物质（TBARS）；（3）影响神经元突触（包括突触前和突触后），随后导致相关记忆功能障碍。相反，木栓酮给药不仅消除了东莨菪碱诱导的氧化应激、胶质细胞激活和神经炎症，还抑制了p-JNK和NF-kappaB及其下游信号分子。此外，木栓酮给药改善了神经元突触，并逆转了东莨菪碱诱导的记忆障碍，同时抑制β-分泌酶（BACE-1）以阻断淀粉样蛋白生成的淀粉样通路。总之，所有结果表明，木栓酮是一种有效的天然分离的神经治疗剂，可逆转东莨菪碱诱导的神经病理，这是阿尔茨海默病的特征。
